sentences.text: Rule twenty-two sets the minimum range at which each light must be visible, and it depends on vessel length.
On vessels fifty meters or more, the masthead light must be visible six miles, and every other light three miles.
On vessels from twelve to fifty meters, the masthead light must be visible five miles, but only three miles if the vessel is under twenty meters.
Sidelights, sternlight, towing light and all-round lights must be visible two miles.
On vessels under twelve meters, the masthead light must be visible two miles, the sidelights one mile, and the sternlight, towing and all-round lights two miles.
The exam asks these numbers often, so make yourself a flashcard.
